events.locality: Cambridge, MA, Cambridge, Massachusetts, US
events.description: Join the LangChain team in Boston (Harvard Square) for an evening of three talks on what it takes to move from prototype to production. You'll hear from Mason Daugherty on the OSS team, and from Eugene Liu and Michael Dik on our Deployed Engineering team, who work with teams on getting agents into production. 🎤 Talk 1: From Prototype to Production: The architectural foundation of production agents with Michael Explore the common themes and challenges when moving AI agents from prototype to production. Learn how to navigate critical considerations like identity, guardrails, evaluations, tool access, and memory to build reliable, secure, and scalable agents. 🎤 Talk 2: Building a Coding Agent Your Team Owns with Mason Mason will walk us through his team's experience building Open SWE and unique challenges in building a coding agent. 🎤 Talk 3: Making Agent Memory Grounded, Traceable, and Useful with Eugene Agents can retrieve facts, but answering complex questions across disconnected sources means remembering how sources connect—and showing the evidence behind what they say. This talk explores how compiled wikis and evidence graphs make agent memory more grounded, traceable, and useful

events.description: AI in Fleet Management A Wunder Mobility Meetup — Hamburg Every operator is being told that AI will transform fleet operations. Far fewer people can tell you which parts already work and which are still a demo with good lighting. That is what this evening is for. We will show what we have actually shipped — where AI is already taking real work out of dispatch, maintenance, pricing and customer support — and we will be just as clear about where it is not ready yet. Then we hand the room over to the operators and builders running their own experiments, so you leave knowing what to adopt now, what to pilot, and what you cannot afford to miss right now while everyone else is still debating it. No product pitch dressed up as a talk. A room of people who run fleets, comparing notes on the tools that are actually moving the numbers. This is an invite-only event for senior leaders and builders in shared mobility. If you are in the room, it is because you belong in the conversation. events.title: LangChain x hackers&wizards Hackathon: Building with Agent Harnesses (Hamburg)
events.locality: Hamburg, Germany, Hamburg, Hamburg, DE
events.description: This hackathon is about building with agent harnesses, hands-on, alongside the people building the tools. We're teaming up with hackers&wizards to host an evening of talks and hacking in Hamburg. You'll form small groups, build a deep agent from scratch, and demo it to a panel of judges by the end of the night. What you'll build The theme is agent harnesses — the scaffolding that turns a model into a system that can plan, use tools, and recover from its own mistakes. Steffen Hausmann will kick things off with two short talks: one on deep agents, and one on managed deep agents. Then you'll put it into practice. A few days before the event, we'll send out a prompt so you can come with an idea already in mind. Use the time before the hackathon to think through your approach — you'll want it once the clock starts. What to bring Your laptop and a group to hack with (we'll help you form one if you don't have one) Your own API keys for any models or tools you plan to use Questions for Steffen, and the hackers&wizards team — they'll be around all night We'll provide LangSmith credits to every attendee for the event, so you can trace and debug your agent as you build. 🏆 Prizes 1st place: $3
